intro: Lesson 8: Replying to the adhan, the iqamah and prayer times. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: Answering the adhan
points: At 'hayya 'ala ...' say: la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah

head: Adhan
Iqamah
rows: Tells us the time has come

box.title: One sentence on answering the adhan

keywords.def: the second call when salah is about to start

keywords.term: la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah
keywords.def: there is no power or strength except with Allah
the set times of the five prayers

questions.q: Explain the difference between the adhan and the iqamah.
questions.a: The adhan says the time has come; the iqamah says the prayer is starting now.

questions.q: Which prayer is just after sunset?
What do we do after the adhan finishes?
Make a 'my prayer day' clock on the pupil PDF: write the five prayers at the right times of day and one sentence on answering the adhan.
questions.a: Fajr dawn, Dhuhr midday, Asr afternoon, Maghrib sunset, Isha night; I repeat the adhan words

questions.q: Extend: which words are added in the iqamah?
Stretch: why might the prayer times change through the year?
questions.a: Sunrise and sunset change with the seasons.

questions.q: What do we say when we hear 'hayya 'ala s-salah'?
options: La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah
questions.a: A) La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah. The Prophet ﷺ taught this reply (Muslim): we ask Allah for the strength to go.

questions.q: Think again: what do we do when we hear the adhan?
questions.a: Repeat the words, say la hawla ... at 'hayya', then make du'a.
